Subject (in full) "V" Movement Chain Letter

Made by C. D. I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by D. S. I. Wilcox

Chain letters in support of the "V" movement are being circulated among local residents through the post.
It is believed that the names and addresses of the recipients are copied from the Telephone Directory.
On 24th August, 1941, a Chinese detective attached to S. I received a chain letter which was mimeographed in the Chinese language. This letter is attached herewith together translation.

August 25, 1941.

Summary translation of a mimeographed letter bearing on
the "V" movement.

August 21, 1941.

Sir,

The "V" movement has been set afoot. "V means
ultimate victory which would be more splendid and glorious
than those won at Crete, Narvik and Dunkirk. The ultimate
victory will represent the
/victory of Christianity, Culture, Democracy and Liberty.
Exemplary in the strife for ultimate victory is the U.S.S.R.

The "V" Movement Lien Nyi Society, which we have
organized for the purpose of promoting the movement, can be
joined by anyone. Members are not required to pay membership
fees; they need only make three copies of this letter and send
them to three of their intimate friends. Should they not
do so, it is feared that Hitler may win, Democratic nations
may lose, and the Nazi Party may rule the world.

This "letter of victory", which was started by General
Wavell, has gone round the Globe once. Shortly afterwards,
great victories were won at Benghazi and Sollum in Greece.

Please join the society because this will also help
You in gaining "victory" in your own business. Will you
Please write three copies of this letter and mail same to your
friends within twenty-four hours. When the letter has gone
round the globe three times, Hitler will surely be defeated.

Beware of the Fifth Column !
(Sender) "For the Sake of Victory",
21/8/41.
page_data.zh:
1941年8月25日。

关于“V”字运动的油印信函译文摘要。

1941年8月21日。

先生：

“V”字运动已经发起。“V”代表最终的胜利，这将比在克里特岛、纳尔维克和敦刻尔克赢得的胜利更加灿烂辉煌。最终的胜利将代表
/基督教、文化、民主和自由的胜利。
在争取最终胜利的斗争中，苏联是典范。

我们为推广该运动而组织了“V”字运动联谊社，任何人均可加入。成员无需缴纳会费；只需将此信抄写三份，寄给三位亲密朋友即可。若不这样做，恐怕希特勒会获胜，民主国家会失败，纳粹党将统治世界。

这封由韦维尔将军发起的“胜利之信”已绕地球一周。此后不久，在希腊的班加西和索卢姆赢得了伟大的胜利。

请加入本社，因为这也将有助于你在自己的事业中获得“胜利”。请在二十四小时内抄写三份此信并寄给你的朋友。当此信绕地球三周时，希特勒必将失败。

警惕第五纵队！
（发信人）“为了胜利”，
21/8/41。

Distribution of Pro-Chungking Handbills at Great
World Amusement Resort, French Concession

Vide Sp.Br.
Report dated
21/7/41.

At 3.30 p.m. July 21, handbills entitled
"Open Letter Addressed by Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek
to People of Friendly Nations" were distributed by some
unknown persons at the Great World Amusement Resort,
No. 1 Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession.

Upon learning of the occurrence, a large party
of detectives and policemen were immediately sent by
the French Police to the scene and conducted searches.
They were assisted by several Japanese Gendarmes in plain
clothes. However, no arrest was made.

At about 5 p.m. all visitors in the amusement
resort were compelled to leave the premises, and the
Great World Amusement Resort was ordered temporarily to
suspend business.

Co. 22/7.

法租界大世界游乐场分发亲重庆传单事宜

参见政治部
1941年7月21日
报告。

7月21日下午3时30分，一些身份不明的人在法租界敏体尼荫路1号大世界游乐场分发了题为《蒋介石委员长致友邦人士公开信》的传单。

得知此事后，法租界警务处立即派出大批探员和警察赶赴现场并进行搜查。几名便衣日本宪兵协助了搜查。然而，未逮捕任何人。

下午5时左右，游乐场内的所有游客被强行要求离开，大世界游乐场被勒令暂时停业。

CONFIDENTIAL
July 21, 1941. 8531

Distribution of National Salvation Propaganda

According to information to hand, local
patriotic elements have prepared a number of lead
typed handbills (printing base unavailable) entitled
"Full text of an open letter addressed by Generalissimo
Chiang Kai Shek to the people of friendly nations" and
purporting to emanate from the "Shanghai Section of
the General Administrative Office of the Central
Cultural Dispatch Station" (中央文化驛站總管理處上海分站)
and will distribute copies of this handbill in the
Western and Central Districts on the afternoon of
July 21 and July 22.

（批：Copies to S.I. / Soul, 22/7）

The handbill, of which a summarized translation
is attached herewith, embodies the following three

page_data.en:
July 21, 1941.

Summarized translation of an open letter addressed by
Generalissimo Chiang Kai-shek to the people of friendly
nations

Four years have elapsed since the outbreak of the
Sino-Japanese hostilities. We recognized at the beginning
that if the invasion was not checked, not only the very
existence of China could be jeopardized but much calamity
would befall the world. Thus, we rose and dealt with
the invaders.

The bitter struggles during the past four years
have now showed effect. We have always been ready to
and
fight to the end/deeply believe that the victory will be
ours. However, if our friendly nations will supply us
with sufficient arms and money, the time of victory
certainly will be accelerated.

The Chinese people fully realize that the ruthless
nature of war and have therefore never desired other nations
to join the war. If justice and righteousness can be upheld
and mankind saved from misfortune, the sacrifices made by
the Chinese people and soldiers will not be made in vain.
This is what I have often repeated.

Rapid changes have taken place in both the
international situation and the situation in the Far East
during the past one year. To-day, the war flames in the
Far East are no longer those of a war between China and
Japan. In fact, complicated relations have been established
the war in Europe and the war in Asia. There is not a single
nation in the world nowadays which can keep herself out of
war. Since the aggressor group have revealed their real
countenance to the world, any nation may become their
objective, sooner or later.
page_data.zh:
1941年7月21日。

蒋介石大元帅致友邦人民公开信的摘要译文

自中日战事爆发以来，已逾四载。吾人于伊始即认识到，若不予以遏制侵略，不仅中国之生存堪忧，世界亦将遭受巨大灾难。因此，我们奋起抗击侵略者。

过去四年的艰苦斗争现已显现成效。我们始终准备战斗到底/深信胜利必将属于我们。然而，若友邦能提供充足的武器与资金，胜利的时刻定能提前到来。

中国人民充分认识到战争的残酷性质，因此从未希望其他国家卷入战争。若能伸张正义，使人类免于祸患，则中国人民与士兵所作的牺牲便不会白费。这是我经常重申的观点。

在过去一年中，国际局势与远东局势均发生了迅速变化。如今，远东的战火已不再仅仅是中日之间的战争。事实上，欧洲战争与亚洲战争之间已建立了复杂的关系。当今世界上没有一个国家能够置身战事之外。既然侵略集团已向世人暴露其真面目，任何国家迟早都可能成为其目标。

page_data.en:
- 2 -

In order to avert war and to diminish the misfortunes
caused by war, as is desired by all countries in the world,
I should be glad to make clear to peoples of our friendly
countries the following three points :-

Firstly, the present war flames in the world were
started when Japan invaded our country at the September 18
Incident. During the past year, Japan has conspired with
Germany and Italy in forming the Triple Alliance and
established her naval bases of aggression on Hainan Island
and in French Indo-China. In fact, not only did Japan
start the war in East Asia but also the present world war.
If she is not defeated, the war in this world can never be
stopped and the people can never live peacefully.

Secondly, if the democratic nations in all Asia,
America and Europe can unite and co-operate under the banner
of anti-aggression, they certainly will win the war. Hence,
our friendly nations should realize the Pacific Ocean is no
less important than the Atlantic Ocean and that the position
of Asia to-day is even more important than that of Europe.
Further, they should be aware that the more serious the
European situation becomes, the quicker Japan's invading
influences should be destroyed. For the sake of the future
of the world, our friendly nations should enforce sanctions
against the war promoter first.

Thirdly, we firmly believe that the total strength
of anti-aggressor nations is much stronger than that of the
invaders. During the present life-and-death struggles, all
our anti-aggressor friendly nations should not have the
slightest jealousy of each other but earnestly co-operate
and take the initiative in attack. If this can be done, the
ultimate victory must be ours. It must be understood that
whenever there is a chance, Japan will venture herself. She
will make use of the hesitant attitude of the democratic
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

为了避免战争并减少战争造成的不幸——这也是世界各国所希望的——我谨向友邦人民阐明以下三点：

第一，当今世界的战火始于日本在“九一八”事变中入侵我国。在过去一年中，日本与德国、意大利勾结，组成三国同盟，并在海南岛及法属印度支那建立了侵略性的海军基地。事实上，日本不仅发动了东亚战争，也发动了当前的世界大战。若不击败日本，世界战争永无停止之日，人民永无安宁之时。

第二，如果亚洲、美洲和欧洲的民主国家能在反侵略的旗帜下团结合作，必将赢得战争。因此，友邦应认识到太平洋的重要性不亚于大西洋，且今日亚洲的地位甚至比欧洲更为重要。此外，他们应意识到，欧洲局势越严峻，就越应迅速摧毁日本的侵略势力。为了世界的前途，友邦应首先对战争发动者实施制裁。

第三，我们坚信，反侵略国家的总力量远强于侵略者。在当前生死存亡的斗争中，所有反侵略的友邦不应彼此存有丝毫猜忌，而应真诚合作，主动发起进攻。若能如此，最终胜利必属我方。必须明白，只要有机会，日本便会铤而走险。它将利用民主国家的犹豫态度，

The present moment when a war has broken between Germany
and Soviet Russia is, indeed, a splendid opportunity
for Japn to realize both her southward and northward
expansion programmes. This is what our friendly nations
must not overlook.

Finally, I should like to say that the Chinese
people will never forget the assistance afforded us by
our friendly countries. China is now having a life-and-
death struggle with Japan. In engaging herself in this
war, China is not only fighting for the extermination
of the aggressive violent forces but also has a desire
to do something for the civilization and happiness of a
free world to come.

The following is the statement of Zung Zeu Chi (陳善繼).

（左侧印章：MUNICIPAL POLICE / [签名] / CHINA BRANCH）

My name is Zung Zeu Chi, age 20, a native of Nanking.
I arrived in Shanghai from Nanking on January 21, 1941, with
the intention of entering the Nan Ching (南菁) School,
Lane 401, 6 Racecourse Road. Through the introduction of my
father Zung Wei Hu (陳為環), who is now in Loh Huh
(六合), Kiangsu, I approached a teacher named Hsu Tse
Wen (許子文) of the above school, who told me to live
in the school premises.

At about 8.30 p.m. January 26, I left the school for
the purpose of doing some shopping. When I proceeded to
Chang Yuan (張園), the former site of Palo Swimming Pool,
on Bubbling Well Road, I met a person named Chu (朱), whom
I had met in the school on several occasions. He asked me to
walk with him, whereupon I followed him in company with three
others whom I do not know.

On the way he requested me to post handbills of an
anti-Wang Ching Wei nature. I asked him what was the use of
of posting such handbills. He told me just to arouse the
people in Shanghai and nothing would happen in doing so, as
he would stand behind me and watch. At the same time he
handed me several copies of the handbills and told me to keep
in my possession.

When we arrived at Bubbling Well Road near Medhurst
and told
Road, Chu handed me another handbill/me to post it on the wall.
I did what he told me and when I was posting the handbill, I
was caught by the Municipal Police. On seeing my arrest by
the Police, my friend and the other male Chinese left behind

我叫陈善继，20岁，南京人。
我于1941年1月21日从南京抵达上海，
打算进入位于跑马厅路6号401弄的南菁学校就读。通过我
父亲陈为环（Zung Wei Hu）的介绍——他目前身在江苏六合——我联系了该校一位名叫许子文（Hsu Tse Wen）的老师，他让我住在校内。

1月26日晚上8点30分左右，我离开学校去
买东西。当我走到静安寺路张园（原巴罗游泳池旧址）时，遇到一个姓朱（Chu）的人，我在学校里曾几次见过他。他叫我跟他一起走，于是我便跟随他，同行的还有另外三个我不认识的人。

途中，他要求我张贴反汪精卫性质的传单。我问他张贴这种传单有什么用。他说只是为了唤起上海民众，这样做不会出事，因为他会在我身后盯着。同时，他递给我几份传单，让我收好。

当我们到达静安寺路靠近麦特赫斯特路的地方时，朱又递给我一份传单，让我把它贴在墙上。我照他说的做了，就在我张贴传单时，被公共租界巡捕抓获。看到我被警察逮捕，我的朋友和其他几名中国男子将

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
P.M.O.
LEGIA JAPAN

My name is Chang hai Ling, female, age 19, a
native of Wusieh, residing at No.41 Dong Kong Li ( 同康里 )
Boulevard de Montigny, French Concession. I am a
student of the Nan Ching ( 南青 ) Middle School, Lane
401, No.6 Race Course Road. I was formerly a student
of the Ai Kuo Middle School, Nanyang Road near Ferry Road,
leaving there after the summer holidays, in 1940.
At about 8 p.m. January 26, at the request
of a school-mate of mine, Cheung Yuan Li ( 莊元禮 ), I
left my home with the intention to proceed to the Roxy
Theatre. On the way on Duoling Well Road near
Ledhurst Road, I saw several persons posting handbills
on electric light poles and walls. When I arrived to
the Roxy Theatre, the tickets were sold out. I then
with my friend returned home via the same route. I
saw the person who posted the handbill arrested by a
Japanese Policeman. As I passed by, I told my Friend
that I had seen the person posting handbills and why he
was arrested. On hearing of my words, the Japanese
Policeman took me into custody together with the male
Chinese, whom I did not know before. I have no connection
with the posting of handbills.
The above is my true statement.

LEGIA JAPAN

我叫张海玲，女，19岁，无锡人，现住法租界蒙太尼路同康里41号。我是跑马厅路6号401弄南青中学的学生。我以前是爱国中学的学生，该校位于斐伦路附近的南阳路，我于1940年暑假后离开该校。
1月26日晚上8点左右，应我的同学庄元礼（Cheung Yuan Li）的要求，我离开家，打算去罗克西大戏院。在前往杜林路（Duoling Well Road，即静安寺路）靠近莱得赫斯特路（Ledhurst Road，即麦特赫斯特路）的途中，我看见几个人在电线杆和墙上张贴传单。当我到达罗克西大戏院时，票已售罄。于是我和朋友沿原路回家。我看见那个张贴传单的人被一名日本警察逮捕。经过时，我对朋友说，我看见有人张贴传单，以及他为何被捕。听到我的话，那名日本警察将我和那名我之前不认识的中国男子一起拘留。我与张贴传单一事毫无关系。
以上是我的真实供词。

page_data.en:
Translation

Copies of a handbill written in Chinese, containing
the following slogans of a national salvation and anti-Wang
Ching Wei nature were found on Dubooling Well Road near
Ledhurst Road on January 26 :

1. Support our leader Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek.
2. Down with the Japanese imperialism.
3. Down with the traitor Wang Ching Wei and his subordinates.
4. Don't read the "poisonous" newspaper - Central China and
New China Daily News, Ling Pao and Sin Shun Pao.
5. Down with those newspaper-men and news reporters willing
to become traitors.
page_data.zh:
译文

1月26日，在靠近莱得赫斯特路（Ledhurst Road）的杜林路（Dubooling Well Road）发现了若干份中文传单的副本，其中包含以下救国及反汪精卫性质的标语：

1. 拥护我们的领袖蒋委员长蒋介石。
2. 打倒日本帝国主义。
3. 打倒汉奸汪精卫及其党羽。
4. 勿阅“毒”报——《华中日报》、《新中国日报》、《灵报》及《新顺报》。
5. 打倒那些甘当汉奸的新闻界人士和记者。

                     Jan. 26th.      41.
1.

Arrest of a male and a female Chinese for posting
Anti-Japanese & Anti-Wang Ching Wei posters.

At 10.15p.m. on the 26-1-41, P.P.S. 719 R. Kusano
and C.P.C. 266 brought to Station the two under-
described persons for posting Anti-Japanese and Anti-
Wang Ching Wei posters on Bubbling Well Road.
(1) Zung Zou Kyi (陳祖繼), 20, Nanking,
    s/student, residing Nan Ching Middle
    School, Zau Kung Li, Race Course Road.
(2) Tsang Hai Ling (張海玲), 19, Wusih,
    s/female, 41 Doong Kong Li, Boulevard
    de Montigny, F/Concession.

Enquiries by the undersigned and C.D.S. 259
ascertained that at 10p.m. even date, the above
police officers whilst patrolling Bubbling Well Road,
observed the 1st named above, in the act of posting
an Anti-Wang Ching Wei poster on the wall of No. 830
Bubbling Well, 4 or 5 other male Chinese being in his
company. On their approach, the 1st named was
apprehended and a total of 29 posters of an Anti-
Wang Ching Wei & Anti-Japanese nature were seized,
some on his person and the rest discarded on the
pavement, the others who were with him making good
their escape.

At this juncture, the 2nd named above appeared
on the scene to investigate the cause of the 1st
named's arrest. Whereupon, she was also taken into
custody and brought to Station for questioning.

（左侧印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH，内有签名）

两名中国人（一男一女）因张贴

1941年1月26日晚上10点15分，巡捕房警员719号 R. Kusano 和华籍巡捕266号将下述两人带至捕房，原因是他们在静安寺路张贴反日和反汪精卫海报。
(1) 陈祖继（Zung Zou Kyi），20岁，南京人，
    学生，住跑马厅路曹公里南菁中学。
(2) 张海玲（Tsang Hai Ling），19岁，无锡人，
    女，住法租界蒙太尼路同康里41号。

经本人与刑事侦缉处259号探员查询，查明当晚10点，上述
警员在静安寺路巡逻时，目睹上述第一名嫌疑人在静安寺路830号的墙上张贴反汪精卫海报，当时另有4或5名中国男子与其在一起。当警员走近时，第一名嫌疑人被抓获，共缴获29张反汪精卫及反日性质的海报，部分在其身上搜出，其余丢弃在人行道上，其他同行者则趁机逃脱。

此时，上述第二名嫌疑人出现在现场，欲了解
第一名嫌疑人被捕的原因。于是，她也被拘留并带至捕房接受讯问。

"918 - The highest spirit of nation and people."
"We must win the victory."
"We must succeed in constructing our nation."
"Down the Japanese bandits."
"Clean all the traitors."

C.D.C.310 made enquiries in the vicinity but
failed to locate any person who witnessed these
slogans being painted on the wall.

Coolies were sent to erase off these slogans.

C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang.

On the morning of August 4, 1940, instructions
were received from D.C. (Crime) through D.D.O. "A"
that the two Chinese male youths named Woo Yuehding
(何月庭) and Fei Vung-ching (費文慶), who
were arrested on August 12, 1940 on Yu Ya Ching
Road near Hankow Road in connection with the chalking
of slogans of a national salvation nature on a
electric pole and the nearby wall, be released
forthwith on the usual guarantee bond.

In the meantime, Woo Tsung Yu (何春裕), a
salesman of the Zuh Sing Zung Cotton Cloth Shop,
French Concession, who is the father of Woo Yueh-ding,
called at Louza Police Station in company with Woo
Lingquin, a lawyer. A guarantee bond in duplicate,
was signed by Woo Yueh ding and witnessed by lawyer Woo,
and consequently Woo Yueh Ding was released at 11.20
a.m. 14-8-40.

At 2 p.m. August 14, 1940, Fei Sung Sz (費沈氏),
mother of Fei Vung Ching, accompanied by one named Li
Ching Piao (李金標), Proprietor of the Ching
Tsong Cardboard box shop, 19 Teh Yui Li, Lloyd Road,
came to the station and offered guarantee for her
son. A guarantee bond in duplicate was accordingly
signed by her and witnessed by Li Ching Piao. Fei
Vung Ching was released at 2.50 p.m. 14-8-40.

Both guarantee bonds are attached to this report.

1940年8月12日在虞洽卿路逮捕两名中国男子，涉及在电线杆及附近墙壁上书写标语。
刑事侦缉督察 施泽良（Sih Tse Liang，音译）。

1940年8月4日上午，通过“A”区副督察长收到犯罪科（Crime）总监的指示，要求立即以通常的保释金释放何月庭（Woo Yuehding）和費文慶（Fei Vung-ching）这两名中国青年男子，他们于1940年8月12日在靠近汉口路的虞洽卿路因在电线杆及附近墙壁上书写救国性质标语而被捕。

在此期间，何月庭的父亲、法租界祖兴庄棉布店（Zuh Sing Zung Cotton Cloth Shop，音译）店员何春裕（Woo Tsung Yu，音译）偕同律师吴林钦（Woo Lingquin，音译）来到老闸捕房。一式两份的保释契据由何月庭签署，并由吴律师见证，因此何月庭于1940年8月14日上午11时20分获释。

1940年8月14日下午2时，費文慶的母亲費沈氏（Fei Sung Sz，音译）在劳埃德路（Lloyd Road）德裕里19号庆丰纸板箱店（Ching Tsong Cardboard box shop，音译）店主李金標（Li Ching Piao，音译）的陪同下来到捕房，为其子提供担保。随即由她签署一式两份的保释契据，并由李金標见证。費文慶于1940年8月14日下午2时50分获释。

两份保释契据均附在本报告后。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
----------------------------------------

The following is the statement of HO YOEK DING (河月庭)
native of Chekiang, taken by D.S.I. Logan
at Louza Station, on the August 12, 1940 and interpreted by Clerk Hsu Ta Yung.
[注：此处有划掉的文字 "Clerk King Sen Chih" 及上方手写的 "translated"]

My name is HO YOEK DING (河月庭), age 25,
native of Chekiang, residing at No. 74 Fah Shiang Tsung
(法翔邨), Rue Perc Frot, French Concession. Since
1933, I have been employed by the Public Works Department
(Land Surveying Department), Shanghai Municipal Council,
as a 'tracer' having been introduced by Mr. Tsang Choeh
Sung (张楚生). Prior to joining the Shanghai
Municipal Council, I studied in the Yoeh Zai Middle
School, Great East Gate, Nantao, for three years, graduating
in 1932. My present pay is $41.00 per mensem.

At 7 a.m. to-day, August 12, 1940, I left my
home for the office. I took a trolley bus to the Great
World Amusement Resort, Boulevard de Montigny and
Avenue Edward VII, where I alighted and partook of some
food from a nearby foodshop. I then continued on foot
on my way to the office via Yu Ya Ching Road but upon
reaching Hankow Road corner, I observed national
salvation slogans written on electric light poles there.
I also noticed a piece of chalk on the roadway which had
evidently been thrown away by somebody. Being
momentarily stirred by patriotic emotions, I picked up
the chalk and wrote the following Chinese characters
on an electric light pole :-

"The Achievement of National Reconstruction
will no doubt be attained!" (建國必成)

Following this, I was arrested by a Chinese
detective (later known to be C.D.S. 316) and was escorted

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
===
警方调查报告。
---

以下是河月庭（HO YOEK DING，即何月庭）的供词，籍贯浙江，由洛根（Logan）侦探副督察长于1940年8月12日在老闸捕房录取，由书记员徐达庸（Hsu Ta Yung）翻译。
[注：此处有划掉的文字 "Clerk King Sen Chih" 及上方手写的 "translated"]

我叫河月庭（HO YOEK DING），年龄25岁，籍贯浙江，居住在法租界贝当路（Rue Perc Frot，即今衡山路）法翔邨74号。自1933年以来，我在上海公共租界工部局公用处（土地测量科）担任‘描图员’，由张楚生（Tsang Choeh Sung）先生介绍入职。在加入上海公共租界工部局之前，我在南市大东门岳哉中学（Yoeh Zai Middle School，音译）就读三年，于1932年毕业。我目前的月薪为41.00元。

今天，1940年8月12日上午7时，我离开家去办公室。我乘坐电车到大世界游乐场，位于蒙太尼路（Boulevard de Montigny，即今嵩山路）和爱德华七世路（Avenue Edward VII，即今延安东路）交汇处，我在那里下车并在附近的一家食品店吃了一些东西。然后我继续步行，经由虞洽卿路前往办公室，但在到达汉口路转角时，我注意到那里的电线杆上写有救国标语。我还注意到路上有一块粉笔，显然是被人扔掉的。出于一时的爱国情感冲动，我捡起粉笔，在一根电线杆上写了以下汉字：-

“建国必成！”

随后，我被一名中国侦探（后知为C.D.S. 316号警员）逮捕，并被押送

My name is FEE WEN CHING (費文慶), aged 21,
unmarried, and a native of Hoopeh. I am at present
residing at No. 41 Foh Ling Lee (福臨里), Rue
of
Lafayette. At the age/13 (1932), I joined the Kiangsu
Provincial Shanghai Middle School and graduated from
same in the summer of 1938; the school premises are
now situated in Rue de Marche. Since my graduation,
I have not obtained any regular employment but served
as a private teacher intermittently, thus making an
income of some $40 a month.

At about 7 o'clock this morning, I happened to
pass by Yu Ya Ching Road near Hankow Road where I
observed posters containing slogans of a national
salvation nature written on walls and electric light
poles. Meanwhile I saw a man obliterating a slogan
on an electric light pole, but I could not see what
the nature of the slogan was as I am near-sighted.
When I went closer with the intention of examining
the characters thereon more clearly, I was arrested
and brought to the Station.

The above is my true statement.

W Logan
D.S.I.

本人名为費文慶，现年21岁，未婚，湖北籍人。目前居住于霞飞路福臨里41号。本人于13岁时（1932年）考入江苏省立上海中学，并于1938年夏从该校毕业；该校校址现位于马浪路。自毕业后，本人未获固定职业，仅断续担任家庭教师，月收入约40元。

今日早晨7时许，本人途经靠近汉口路的亚尔培路时，看见墙壁及电灯杆上贴有含有救国性质标语的海报。同时，本人看见一名男子正在擦除电灯杆上的一条标语，但因本人近视，未能看清该标语的具体内容。当本人走近意图更清楚地查看上面的文字时，即被逮捕并带至捕房。

以上系本人真实供词。

Misc. 534/40.
Lou. 8831
12-8-40/2 8 40

Arrest of two male Chinese on Yu Ya Ching Road on 12-8-40 in connection with chalking of slogans on a electric pole and the nearby wall.

C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang.

At 6.30 a.m. August 12, 1940, a report was received from Inspector Boorman to the effect that at the corner of Yu Ya Ching Road and Hankow Roads several slogans were found chalked on an electric pole and the nearby wall.

C.D.S. 316 and Coolie No. 86 were detailed to proceed to the scene, where it was found that the slogans in question, when translated read as follows:-

(1) On the Electric Pole:
"Be successful in constructing our country!"

(2) On the nearby wall:
"We would rather be a broken jade than a complete tile!"
"To support our Chief Executive Chiang in fighting to the end!"

Coolie No. 86 was in the act of washing the characters off when a male Chinese named Woo Yueh Ding came to the scene and re-wrote with chalk the slogan:

"Be successful in constructing our country".

On observing this, C.D.S. 316 took him into custody. Another male Chinese named Fei Vung Ching approached the coolie who was washing the characters off the wall, and tried to prevent the coolie from carrying on. C.D.S. 316 intervened and also took him into custody. Both were later brought to the Station for questioning.

Woo Yueh Ding (何月定) 25, Chekiang, S/clerk,
page_data.zh:
杂项 534/40。
老闸 8831
12-8-40/2 8 40

1940年8月12日，两名中国男子因在亚尔培路的一根电灯杆及附近墙壁上书写粉笔标语而被捕。

刑事侦缉督察 施子良（Sih Tse Liang）。

1940年8月12日上午6时30分，接布曼（Boorman）巡官报告称，在亚尔培路与汉口路转角处，发现一根电灯杆及附近墙壁上用粉笔写有数条标语。

刑事侦缉警士 316号及苦力 86号奉命前往现场，经查，所涉标语译意如下：

(1) 在电灯杆上：
“建国成功！”

(2) 在附近墙壁上：
“宁为玉碎，不为瓦全！”
“拥护蒋总裁抗战到底！”

当苦力 86号正在清洗这些字迹时，一名名叫何月定（Woo Yueh Ding）的中国男子来到现场，并用粉笔重新书写了标语：

“建国成功”。

见此情形，刑事侦缉警士 316号将其拘捕。另一名名叫費文慶（Fei Vung Ching）的中国男子走近正在清洗墙壁字迹的苦力，试图阻止其继续工作。刑事侦缉警士 316号介入干预，并将其一并拘捕。两人随后均被带至捕房接受讯问。

何月定（Woo Yueh Ding），25岁，浙江籍，下级职员，

page_data.en:
Surveying Office P.W.D., residing 74 Soong Pah Tsung
Route due Pere Proe, stated that he was on the way
to his office and when passing Yu Ya Ching Road he
observed the coolie erasing the slogan from the
electric pole. Overcome with his patriotic feelings
he went near and by means of a piece of chalk which
he found at the foot of the electric pole rewrote
the slogan. He denied having written the original
slogan, or having any knowledge of the person who
wrote it.

The 2nd man taken into custody gave his name as
Fei Vung Ching(費文慶) 21, Hoopeh, teacher, residing
41 Foh Ling Lee Route Lafayette, when questioned
he stated he was on the way from his home to the Yah
Kung Supplementary School, corner of Kiangsi and
Hankow Roads; when passing Yu Ya Ching Road near
Hankow Road he saw the coolie washing out the slogans
chalked on the wall. He approached the coolie and,
attempted to stop him, claiming he was anxious to
see what the slogans were but denied having any
intention to prevent the coolie from erasing them.
He denied having written the slogans on the wall and
also stated he did not see any person write same.
A search of his person failed to produce any chalk.

With the assistance of the French Police, visits
were made by C.D.S. 130, D.S.I. Suhoff and the
undersigned to the homes of the two above mentioned
men but nothing of a suspicious nature was found and
page_data.zh:
任职于工务局测量处，居住于贝当神父路宋帕宗路74号，声称当时正前往办公室，途经亚尔培路时，看见苦力正在擦除电灯杆上的标语。出于爱国热情，他走上前去，利用在电灯杆脚下找到的一截粉笔，重新书写了该标语。他否认书写了原始标语，也声称不知晓书写者为何人。

第二名被拘捕男子自称費文慶（Fei Vung Ching）（費文慶），21岁，湖北籍，教师，居住于霞飞路福臨里41号，受讯时声称，他当时正从家中前往位于江西路与汉口路转角的雅公补习学校；途经靠近汉口路的亚尔培路时，看见苦力正在清洗写在墙上的粉笔标语。他走近苦力并试图阻止，声称急于查看标语内容，但否认有意阻止苦力擦除标语。他否认在墙上书写了标语，并称未看见任何人书写。对其人身搜查未发现任何粉笔。

在法租界警方的协助下，刑事侦缉警士 130号、副督察长苏霍夫（Suhoff）及签署人走访了上述两人的住所，但未发现任何可疑物品，且

page_data.en:
and no papers showing they were connected with any
political party were found.
Their fingerprints were checked by the Finger
Print Bureau both show no criminal records.
The result of the enquiries were communicated
to the D.C. Crime who gave instructions that the
two men be detained until 15-8-40 when he would
consider their disposal.

Re.Slogan of an anti-Japanese Nature scribbled on
the pane of window-glass at No.97 Jinkee Road.

At 10.40a.m.25-5-40 a telephone message was
received from Mr.H.Ogino,Room No.54,119 Jinkee Road to
the effect that an anti-Japanese slogan was written on
the pane of window-glass of the premises situated
opposit his office.

C.D.C.175 and the undersigned proceeded to the
scene and ascertained the following:-

Chinese characters "抗戰 War of Resistance" had
been scribbled in chalk on the pane of window glass of
Room No.2 on the 3rd floor of the premises at No.97
Jinkee Road,the room being the dormitory of the Chinkiang
Middle School which occupy the entire 3rd floor rooms of
these premises.

Detectives brought the matter to the attention of
Mr.Sung Yih Juh(沈亦珍),the principal,who stated that
he did not know when or by whom it had been scribbled.

The slogan in question was immediately erased by
one of the school coolies.

Date May 9th, 1940.

REPORT

Subject Re Slogan chalked on a wall.

Made by. D.S. 103 Baldock. Forwarded by Officer i/c.

Sir,

At 4 p.m. on the 9/5/40 Supt. Yao Kia Sui (姚家瑞) telephoned this station and reported that there was a slogan chalked in Chinese characters on a wall on the West side of Hart Road near Singapore Road reading as follows:-

"Zung Ts Woo (陳志和) is a traitor and will be shot."

Enquiries in the vicinity by C.D.C. 331 and D.S. 103 Baldock failed establish the identity of the person responsible for writing the slogan, or the person Zung Ts Woo referred to in same.

The wall on which the slogan was written surrounds the Gonzaga College grounds.

The writing has been washed off by a station coolie, and a copy of this report is forwarded to the Special Branch.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Baldock
D.S. 103.

Subject National Salvation Propaganda

Made by/ and Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

Copies of a coloured slip of a national
salvation and anti-Wang Ching Wei nature
purporting to have emanated from the "Shanghai
Municipality Various Circles United Traitor-
Extermination Corps (上海市各界联合锄奸团)"
were found on Hooper Road near Chekiang Road
at 7.50 p.m. April 28, 1940. There is no
record of such an organisation in Special Branch
records.

Copies of a coloured pamphlet of a
similar nature purporting to have emanated from
the "Propaganda Department of the Shanghai
Municipality General Labour Union (上海市总工会宣传部)"
were found at 3 p.m. April 30, 1940 on Kiangse
Road near Foochow Road.

The Shanghai Municipality General Labour
Union was inaugurated in December, 1931 by the
defunct local Kuomintang Headquarters but
suspended its functions in November 1937 when
the Chinese Forces withdrew from Shanghai.
There is no information that this labour union
has resumed and it would appear that patriotic
elements are using the name for propaganda
purposes.

Specimen copies of the pamphlet and slip
are attached hereto together with translation.

G. Crawford

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 1. Special Branch
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. 5 D...... Date April 10 1940）

Subject Anti-Wang Ching Wei handbill mailed to Chinese staff of
Central Police Station.

Made by.D.S.I. Kao Yen Ken. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

At 10 a.m. April 9, a letter was received
through the post at the Central Police Station,
addressed to the Chinese staff in general. It contains
a mimeographed handbill of an anti-Wang Ching Wei nature,
a full translation of which is attached.

According to the post mark, the missive
was posted at 8 p.m. April 8 at the Seymour Road Sub-
Station of the Chinese Post Office. It is signed in
the name of "The Woosung-Shanghai Special Martial Law
Department of the Traitor Mopping-up Headquarters of
the Military Affairs Commission of the National
Government" which is new to Special Branch.

Copies of a similar letter have also been
received by a number of local schools.

（批：6%）

Kao Yen Kin
D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch)
（批：Rd / 10/4）

（印：RECEIVED BY (S.B.) REGISTRY DATE / 2 / 11 / 40）

报告
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特别处 登记号 5 D ____ 日期 1940年4月10日）

事由：寄给中央捕房华籍职员的反汪精卫传单。

制作人：高级探员 高延肯 (Kao Yen Ken)。转呈人：督察 克劳福德 (Crawford)。

4月9日上午10时，中央捕房通过邮政收到一封信件，收件人为全体华籍职员。信中附有一份油印的反汪精卫性质传单，全文译文见附件。

根据邮戳显示，该信件于4月8日晚8时在中国邮局西摩路支局投寄。落款署名为“国民政府军事委员会锄奸总部淞沪特别戒严司令部”，此名称为特别处此前所未闻。

当地多所学校也收到了类似信件的副本。

（批：6%）

高延肯 (Kao Yen Kin)
高级探员。

副督察（特别处）
（批：阅 / 4月10日）

（印：特别处登记室 收到日期 / 1940年11月2日）

page_data.en:
Translation

Traitor Wang is working against the nation and
has surrendered to the enemy. He has sold the interests
of the Chinese race for selfish ends, and is opposed by
God and human beings alike. He is now openly establishing
a puppet government under the point of the enemy's bayonet.
He has concluded a secret agreement which is prejudicial
to the national rights and which, once put into effect,
will place the Chinese Race in such a position that it will
be impossible to throw off the enemy's yoke for thousands
of generations to come.

Such treacherous acts on the part of traitor Wang
can in no way suggest the least alteration in the plan for
the war of resistance against the enemy, formulated by
the supreme command. His contemptable demeanor shows his
entire lack of integrity and conscientiousness, and is a
disgrace to the Chinese people.

We believe that hot-blooded fellow-brothers will
never fall into his trap. We must peel his skin as a
punishment in order to pacify the indignation of the public.
You are hereby earnestly urged to unite together whole-
heartedly and participate in the "Traitor-Mopping-Up
Movement" and pledge to annihilate the traitors in order
to avenge the death of the martyrs. You are also urged to
support General Chiang in maintaining of the War of
Resistance with the firm belief that the final victory
will be ours.

Long live the Chinese Republic!
Long live Generalissimo Chiang Kai Shek!

Signed : The Woosung-Shanghai Special
Martial Law Department of the
traitor Mopping Up H.Q. of the
Military Affairs Commission of
the National Government.
page_data.zh:
译文

汪逆祸国殃民，投降敌人。他为了一己私利出卖中华民族的利益，为人神所共愤。他如今在敌人的刺刀胁迫下公开建立傀儡政府。他签订了一项损害国家主权的秘密协定，一旦实施，将使中华民族陷入万世无法摆脱敌人枷锁的境地。

汪逆的这种叛国行径，丝毫不能改变最高统帅部制定的对敌抗战计划。他那卑鄙的行径显示其完全缺乏廉耻和良知，是中国人民的耻辱。

我们相信热血同胞绝不会落入他的圈套。我们必须剥他的皮以作为惩罚，从而平息公众的愤怒。特此恳切呼吁大家同心协力，参加“锄奸运动”，并宣誓歼灭汉奸，以告慰烈士在天之灵。同时也呼吁大家支持蒋将军坚持抗战，坚信最后胜利属于我们。

中华民国万岁！
蒋中正委员长万岁！

署名：国民政府军事委员会锄奸总部
淞沪特别戒严司令部。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Anti-Wang Ching Wei Slogan found written on electric pole in Pootoo Road District.

At 6:20 p.m. 30.3.40., F.P.S. 731 Tsurukuma reported to the station to the effect that an Anti-Wang Ching Wei slogan was found to have been written in chalk on an electric pole on Macao Road near Gordon Road.

C.D.C. 340 was despatched to the scene and copied down the characters, which when translated reads as follows:-

Down with the traitor Wang Zau Ming (汪兆銘).
(打倒漢奸汪兆銘).

Investigations made by detectives in the vicinity failed to elicit any information which would lead to the identity of the person responsible for writing the slogan.

Slogan washed off by station coolie.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Anti-Wang Ching Wei slogans stamped on tramway rails along Weihaiwei Road.

At 9 a.m. 23/3/40 a telephone message was received from Shell House to the effect that anti-Wang Ching Wei slogans were stamped on tramway standards along Weihaiwei Road near Chengtu Road.

D.I. Hill, D.S. Taylor and P.D.7. 160 attended and found that rubber stamp impressions of the "Kuomintang emblem about 4½" in diameter, the centre of which bore Chinese characters translated as follows :- "Wang Ching Wei is a big traitor who surrenders himself to the enemy and sells the country" were stamped on tramway rails all along Weihaiwei Road.

The Special Branch were informed and it was learned that there had been no previous report of this type of propaganda.

The Senior Detective communicated with the D.O. "A" and pointed out that owing to the expected early inauguration of the New Central Government in Nanking there was likely to be a recurrence of anti-Wang Ching Wei propaganda campaigns in the Settlement but in view of Divisional Memo dated 28/9/39 no message had been circulated to warn duties to be on the look-out for persons posting or distributing political propaganda. page_data.en:
Translation of handbill copies which were found
distributed at the corner of Nanking Road and Yu
Ya Ching Road, and Nanking Road and Kwangse Road
corner on August 2 and 3, 1939.

The saying that "Every individual is responsible for
the rise or fall of the nation" has become a watchword for
every one of us. Twenty seven or twenty eight months have
already elapsed since July 7, 1937 when the War of Resistance
commenced. While increasingly larger territories are being
occupied by the enemy, who is penetrating deeper and deeper
into our vast interior, we are drawing nearer and nearer to
our victory.

Since the "Isolated Island" became a part of the Lost
Territory, many of our conscientious youths have awakened to
their responsibilities towards this war of resistance and have
voluntarily left for the interior in order to dedicate their
lives to their country, and to the cause of racial emancipa-
tion. They are giving the enemy blow for blow. On the other
hand, there are still a number of our youths who remain in the
Isolated Island, intoxicating themselves with wine and women,
wasting their energy and money, and dancing under the very
bayonet of the enemy. Never a thought comes to them of the
blood that is being shed daily by the officers and men at the
front for their 450,000,000 brethren. There are also trai-
torous merchants, running dogs of the enemy, who have sold
their national interest and even their own conscience for their
selfish ends. They are transporting enemy goods for sale in
China, so that the enemy may use the money thus derived to
manufacture bombs for bombing over villages and killing our
people. Every conscientious individual should ask him or
herself whether he or she still considers himself or herself
a Chinese; whether he is still intoxicating himself with wine
and women; whether he has become a running dog of the enemy,
page_data.zh:
1939年8月2日和3日在南京路与虞洽卿路路口、以及南京路与广西路路口发现并散发的传单副本译文。

“天下兴亡，匹夫有责”这句话已成为我们每个人的座右铭。自1937年7月7日抗战爆发以来，已过去了二十七或二十八个月。虽然敌人占领的领土越来越大，并日益深入我们广大的内地，但我们正越来越接近胜利。

自从“孤岛”成为沦陷区的一部分以来，许多有良知的青年已经觉醒，认识到自己在抗战中的责任，并自愿前往内地，将生命奉献给国家和民族解放事业。他们正在给予敌人迎头痛击。另一方面，仍有一些青年留在孤岛，沉溺于酒色，浪费精力和金钱，在敌人的刺刀下跳舞。他们从未想到前线官兵每天为他们四亿五千万同胞所流的鲜血。还有一些奸商，即敌人的走狗，为了私利出卖国家利益甚至自己的良心。他们运输敌货在中国销售，以便敌人利用由此获得的资金制造炸弹，轰炸村庄并杀害我们的人民。每一个有良知的人都应该问自己，是否还认为自己是中国人；是否还在沉溺于酒色；是否已成为敌人的走狗，

page_data.en:
- 2 -

and, whether he is selling enemy goods.

Chiang, the Chief Executive, has urged every one
of his compatriots to do his part, calling upon the whole
nation to bear in mind that we will ultimately emerge
triumphant in a protracted war of resistance, towards
which we are to give every ounce of our energy and every
cent of our wealth.

Kiangsu-Chekiang Border Areas Guerilla
Commander in command of the 5th Column
of the 3rd Section of the 4th Independent
Corps.
page_data.zh:
- 2 -

以及是否在销售敌货。

蒋委员长敦促每一位同胞尽自己的一份力，号召全国人民牢记，我们将在持久的抗战中最终取得胜利，为此我们要贡献每一分力量和每一分钱财富。

江浙边区游击司令
第三纵队第五支队
第四独立大队指挥官。

With reference to the anti-Japanese handbills
which purport to have been issued by the "Propaganda
Section of the China Youths Anti-Japanese and National
Salvation Volunteer Corps" and which were distributed
in large quantities in outside roads area in the
Western District and in thoroughfares in the Settlement
on May 7 and 8, 1939, searching enquiries have been
made by detectives attached to this office with a view
to locating the publisher but without result.
Numerous printing shops in the Settlement have been
visited in an endeavour to discover the establishment
responsible for the printing of the handbills but
efforts in this direction have also proved unsuccessful
due to the fact that the types used in the printing of
the handbills are similar to those commonly used by
almost all the printing presses in Shanghai.
The China Youths Anti-Japanese and National
Salvation Volunteer Corps has not come to the notice
of the police since May 8, the date on which the
handbills were distributed in the Settlement and it
is therefore believed that the organization was but
one of mushroom type and is no longer in existence.

Liao Chung Chien
D. S. I.
D.C. (Special Branch)

Translation of a handbill, copies of which
were found by the Japanese Military at the
entrance to the N.Y.K. and O.S.K. wharves,
Yangtzepoo Road, on the night of June 20, 1939.

Letter to Chinese Brethren

Dear Chinese brethren!

Your "bitter enemy" and a number of traitors
who are without conscience, have organized the so-called
"Hwa Hsing Bank" for the purpose of disturbing war time
finances and exchange and issue worthless paper for your
legal tender. With the money thus obtained, they will
establish larger gambling dens to serve as traps for the
Chinese people. Chinese brethren! You must be determined
in your plans to upset their schemes and kill the "ape-
man" (Japan). Chinese brethren! Do you know what happened
to the notes of the Federal Reserve Bank in North China?
The Bank has made every effort to circulate its notes but
without result.

Keep this in mind! You must not accept such
worthless bank notes. If you accept one such note, it means
that you fire one more shot at the brave warriors fighting
at the front, that you shoot at your heart with an arrow,
that you destroy your ancestors' tombs, or that you give up
your wives and sisters for their pleasure. To be in posses-
sion of such a bank note is the same as being in possession
of worthless paper and to use the note means you dig a grave
for yourself.

Chinese brethren! Awaken and refrain from
accepting such worthless notes which are practically warrants
issued by the "God of Death". If you do so, you assist your
government in the war of resistance and national reconstruction.

From your Supporters.
page_data.zh:
1939年6月20日晚，日军在杨树浦路（Yangtzepoo Road）日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）和大阪商船会社（O.S.K.）码头入口处发现的传单副本译文。

致中国同胞书

亲爱的中国同胞们！

你们的“死敌”和一些没有良心的汉奸组织了所谓的“华兴银行”，目的是扰乱战时金融和汇兑，并发行毫无价值的纸币作为你们的法定货币。利用由此获得的资金，他们将建立更大的赌场，作为陷害中国人的陷阱。中国同胞们！你们必须下定决心破坏他们的阴谋，杀死“猿人”（日本）。中国同胞们！你们知道华北联邦储备银行的钞票发生了什么吗？该银行竭尽全力流通其钞票，但未获成功。

记住这一点！你们绝不能接受这种毫无价值的钞票。如果你们接受一张这样的钞票，就意味着你们向在前线英勇作战的战士多开了一枪，意味着你们用箭射向自己的心脏，意味着你们毁坏了祖先的坟墓，或者意味着你们将自己的妻妹拱手让人取乐。持有这样的钞票等同于持有废纸，而使用这张钞票意味着你们在为自己挖掘坟墓。

中国同胞们！觉醒吧，不要接受这些实际上是由“死神”签发的毫无价值的钞票。如果你们这样做，就是在协助政府进行抗战和国家重建。

来自你们的支持者。

page_data.en:
Translation of a pamphlet copies of which were
thrown from the roof garden of the Wing On Company
into Chekiang Road on the afternoon of May 18, 1939.

Dear brethren on the "Isolated Island";

When you come to think of your parents, families,
brothers, sisters, relatives and friends and realize that
they are being cruell put to death, subjected to merciless
oppression or forced to wander about aimlessly by the ruth-
less enemy, you will certainly feel exceedingly indignant
and be obsessed with a burning desire to avenge their death
and suffering. This is a problem that deeply concerns
every patriot. To satisfy this desire, we have formed
ourselves into a group, because we are not willing to be
slaves and can not bear to see the iron heels of the enemy
overrunning our national territory; we are determined to
engage the enemy in a life and death encounter, blow for
blow. A part of our group has now arrived at the suburbs
of Shanghai. Bolstered up with the instructions and
encouragement of our supreme leader, Generalissimo Chiang,
we are prepared to practice the creeds of the National
Spiritual General Mobilization at a time when the National
Spiritual General Mobilization Movement is being promoted
everywhere in the country.

Primarily we are armed forces coming from the
field in the guerilla areas of Kiangsu and Chekiang and
our organization has been formed for the purpose of self-
defence and resisting the atrocious Japanese aggression.
Apart from checking invasion by offerring resistance to
the enemy, we also have to maintain constant communication
with other guerilla units so that our resistance may be more
effective. While we are satisfied with the fact that we
have done our part towards the state in the past year, we
have also been convinced that our task ahead requires
page_data.zh:
1939年5月18日下午从永安公司屋顶花园抛入浙江路的传单副本译文。

“孤岛”上的亲爱的同胞们：

当你们想到父母、家人、兄弟、姐妹、亲戚和朋友正被残忍的敌人残酷杀害、遭受无情压迫或被迫四处流浪时，你们一定会感到极度愤怒，并充满为他们报仇雪恨的强烈渴望。这是每个爱国者深切关注的问题。为了满足这一愿望，我们组成了这个团体，因为我们不愿做奴隶，也无法忍受敌人的铁蹄践踏我们的国土；我们决心与敌人进行生死搏斗，以牙还牙。我们的一部分人员现已抵达上海郊区。在我们最高领袖蒋介石委员长的指示和鼓励下，我们准备在全国推广国民精神总动员运动之际，践行国民精神总动员的信条。

我们主要是来自江苏和浙江游击区战场的武装部队，我们的组织是为了自卫和抵抗残暴的日本侵略而成立的。除了通过抵抗敌人来遏制入侵外，我们还必须与其他游击队保持经常联系，以使我们的抵抗更加有效。虽然我们对过去一年为国家尽了一份力感到满意，但我们也深信，我们未来的任务需要

page_data.en:
(2)

the following points to be realised:-

1. To turn the whole population of the guerilla areas
in Kiangsu and Chekiang into powerful forces for
self-defence and resisting the Japanese.

2. To make the population in the guerilla areas in
Kiangsu and Chekiang practice the principles of
the People's Spiritual General Movement and the
procedure governing Their Enforcement.

3. To secure the absolute and unquestionable support
of the people in the guerilla areas in Kiangsu
and Chekiang for the supreme leader and the
national policy in the war of resistance.

4. To further strengthen the organization and training
of the various guerilla units in the guerilla
areas in Kiangsu and Chekiang.

5. To assist the provincial governments of Kiangsu
and Chekiang to restore the administrative system
in the guerilla areas under their jurisdiction.

6. To build an economic foundation aiming at self-
sufficiency in the guerilla areas in Kiangsu and
Chekiang.

To strive for the success of the above task
is the sacred and important duty of the guerilla units
in the guerilla areas. It will not only be a fatal
blow to the enemy in the Eastern Front, but will also
prove to be an important factor in attaining an early
final victory for the war of resistance.

This is a most critical period for the
Chinese race in its history of over 4,000 years, and
in view of the heavy responsibilities ahead of us, only
unwavering faith and undaunted spirit are by no means
page_data.zh:
(2)

认识到以下几点：-

1. 将江苏和浙江游击区的全体民众转化为强大的自卫和抗日力量。

2. 使江苏和浙江游击区的民众实践国民精神总动员运动的原则及其实施程序。

3. 确保江苏和浙江游击区民众对最高领袖及抗战国策给予绝对且毋庸置疑的支持。

4. 进一步加强江苏和浙江游击区各游击队的组织和训练。

5. 协助江苏和浙江省政府恢复其管辖下游击区的行政体系。

6. 建立旨在实现江苏和浙江游击区自给自足的经济基础。

争取上述任务的成功是游击区各游击队神圣而重要的职责。这不仅将对东线敌人造成致命打击，也将证明是实现抗战早日最终胜利的重要因素。

这是中华民族四千多年历史上最关键的时期，鉴于我们肩负的重任，仅有坚定的信念和大无畏的精神绝非

sufficient. It is imperative that our dear brethren
now remaining in the "Isolated Island", especially the
scholars, property owners, financiers, chemists,
engineers and cultural leaders, should effect close and
sincere cooperation so that a satisfactory result may
be achieved in our endeavours to bring about a military
victory. It is earnestly hoped that our dear brethren
in Shanghai will render us guidance and assistance for
completing the task of national reconstruction and the
success of the war of resistance.

Found on Nanking and Chekiang Roads corner at 2.40 p.m. 18.5.39
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

孤島上的親愛同胞們！

當你們聽到我們的消息時，我們知道你們一定很關心我們的行動。我們是江蘇人民抗日自衛軍總指揮部政治部。我們這次來到上海，是為了宣傳抗戰，動員民眾，並且組織游擊隊，在敵後進行武裝鬥爭。我們相信，只要大家團結一致，堅持抗戰到底，最後的勝利一定是屬於我們的。

我們在這裡，看到了許多熱心的同胞，他們願意為祖國貢獻自己的力量。這使我們感到非常欣慰。我們也知道，在上海這個孤島上，生活是很艱難的，但是我們不能因為困難而放棄抗戰。我們要利用一切機會，打擊敵人，保衛家鄉。

我們希望所有的同胞們，都能夠起來，參加到抗戰的行列中來。無論你是工人、學生、商人，還是其他職業，都可以為抗戰做出貢獻。我們可以出錢，出力，或者提供情報。只要我們齊心協力，就一定能夠打敗日本侵略者。

最後，我們呼籲所有的同胞們，不要忘記我們的祖國正在遭受苦難。我們要時刻準備着，為祖國的解放而戰鬥。讓我們攜手並肩，共同爭取最後的勝利！

一、本軍係江蘇人民抗日自衛軍，奉命在敵後開展游擊戰爭，保衛家鄉，打擊日寇。
二、本軍歡迎所有愛國同胞加入，共同抗敵。
三、本軍紀律嚴明，不拿群眾一針一線，請廣大同胞放心。
四、本軍將堅決執行抗戰建國綱領，為實現三民主義而奮鬥。
五、本軍呼籲各界同胞，躍捐輸，支援前線。
六、本軍誓與日寇血戰到底，不成功，成仁！

我們相信，在偉大的民族解放戰爭中，我們一定能夠取得最後的勝利。讓我們高舉抗戰的旗幟，前進！

江蘇人民抗日自衛軍總指揮部政治部

Subject (in full). Anti-Japanese Slogans on Ichang Road.

Made by D.S.I. Burton. Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕** Inspt. i/c.

Sir,

At 11 a.m. on the 13.5.39. P.S. 735 Section 2.
reported to the station that slogans of an Anti-Japanese
nature were written in white chalk and black ink on the
wall of No. 96 Ichang Road, property of the Sung Sing No.
2 Cotton Mill.

C.D.C. 124 proceeded to the point and copied
down the characters: (大中国加！) which when translated
reads:- Great China fights the Japanese.

Enquiries were made in the vicinity in an
effort to locate the writer without success.

A search of the district was made but no
other slogans were found.

Slogans washed off the property by station
coolie.

D.S.I.

D.D.O. "B" Division.

An epistle to the people of Shanghai by the
China Youths Anti-Japanese and National
Salvation Volunteer Corps

Dear Brethren:

Almost twenty months have elapsed since Shanghai
fell into Japanese control, during which period we
have been living like slaves and suffering oppression
in various disguises. Hundreds of lives of our
brethren have been sacrificed through the enemy's
gunfire while a countless number of our sisters have
been raped by the enemy. Our once peaceful and
prosperous homesteads have been invaded and become
scorched earth, while those who have been a little
more fortunate than others in escaping death at the
hands of the enemy, are now wanderers, unemployed and
homeless. It is the duty of us all who are the
scions of Emperor Huang Ti and sons and daughters
of China, to exact a price from the enemy and demand
vengeance. The soldiers at the front are continually
giving up their lives in the war of resistance for
the eternal peace and emancipation of the Chinese race.
As a result of their heroic sacrifices, the war
situation has now taken a turn for the better and in
our favour.

The general counter-offensive has already
commenced and the day is not far distant when we will
see the general collapse of the enemy. While the
general counter-offensive is in progress, the people
page_data.zh:

传单副本译文。

中国青年抗日救国
义勇团致上海同胞书

各位同胞：

上海沦陷于日本控制之下已近二十个月，在此期间，我们
如奴隶般生活，遭受各种伪装的压迫。数百名
同胞的生命牺牲于敌人的炮火之下，无数姐妹
遭敌人强奸。我们曾经和平繁荣的家园被入侵，变为
焦土，而那些比他人稍幸运、未在敌人手中丧生的人，
如今流离失所，失业且无家可归。作为黄帝子孙和中华儿女，
我们所有人都有责任向敌人索取代价并要求复仇。前线
士兵为了中华民族的永久和平与解放，在抗战中不断
献出生命。由于他们的英勇牺牲，战局现已好转，
有利于我方。

全面反攻已经开始，敌人全面崩溃的日子
已不远矣。在全面反攻进行之际，民众

page_data.en:
(2)

of Shanghai should hold themselves in readiness
for eventual participation in a mission of
restoring Greater Shanghai, which has been
occupied for the last twenty months.    There are
many youths leading a life of dissipation in this
city and it is high time we awakened them.    In
view of this great task before us, it is imperative
that they discontinue their life of ease.    Let us
shout the following slogans :-
    (1) Down with Japanese imperialism!.
    (2) Execute by shooting the renegade Wang Ching
        Wei who has sold his country!
    (3) Execute by shooting of all treacherous traitors!
    (4) All citizens of this city!    Unite for the
        recovery of Greater Shanghai!
    (5) Long live the Republic of China!
    (6) Long live Generalissimo Chiang!

                    Issued by the Propaganda Section
                    of the China Youths Anti-Japanese
                    and National Salvation Volunteer
                    Corps.
page_data.zh:
(2)

上海市民应做好准备，以便最终参与
恢复已被占领二十个月的大上海的使命。
本市有许多青年过着放荡的生活，现在是
唤醒他们的时候了。鉴于我们面前的这项伟大任务，
他们必须停止安逸的生活。让我们高呼以下口号：
    (1) 打倒日本帝国主义！
    (2) 枪决卖国贼汪精卫！
    (3) 枪决所有汉奸卖国贼！
    (4) 本市全体市民！团结起来收复大上海！
    (5) 中华民国万岁！
    (6) 蒋委员长万岁！

                    由中国青年抗日救国
                    义勇团宣传部
                    发布

中國青年抗日救國義勇團敬告上海全體民衆書

親愛的同胞們：
自從上海淪陷後到現在已將二十多月了，在這時期中我們過着奴隸般的生活，嘗盡着敵人種種壓迫的
痛苦，無數的同胞在敵人炮彈底下犧牲了生命，無數的姊妹在受着敵人獸性的蹂躪，昔日我們安居樂業的
家園，現在已遭受侵略者炮火的洗禮，變成一片焦土了，倖沒有遭到敵人槍炮屠殺的同胞，現在亦都變
成無業無家的流浪者了，這種不共戴天之仇，這筆數不盡的血債，凡是黃帝的子孫，中華的兒女，誰都有
向敵人報復和索取的責任，所以前線的將士們冒着敵人的炮火浴血抗戰，拚着生命前仆後繼，都是為爭取
我們中華民族生命的永存和解放啊！現在抗戰的勢形，已轉入我們有利的局勢了。
全面總反攻開始發動，敵人離總崩潰的日期已不遠，在這總反攻的時間內，上海每個同胞都應該砥礪
發奮響應前線的戰士，站在自己的崗位上負起收復淪陷已二十個月的大上海的使命，一部份醉生夢死，終
日沉迷在燈紅酒綠的青年們，現在你們應該趕快的覺悟了！不能再過着苟安偷生的生活了！你們都應該動
員起來，做一個收復大上海的戰士啊！最後我們聯合着上海全體的同胞高呼着下面的口號。

（一）打倒日本帝國主義！
（二）槍斃叛黨賣國的汪精衛！
（三）槍斃一切禍國殃民的漢奸！
（四）全體市民聯合起來收復大上海！
（五）中華民國萬歲！
（六）蔣委員長萬歲！

中國青年抗日救國義勇團宣傳組發

Subject (in full). Anti-Japanese Slogans on Robison Road.

Made by D.S.I. Burton. Forwarded by [Signature] Inspt. i/c.

Sir,

At 10 a.m. on the 5.5.39. F.S. 750 Section (2)
reported to the station that slogans of an Anti-Japanese
nature were written in white chalk on the iron gate of
No. 21 Robison Road, property of the Bank of Chosen.

C.D.S. 113 proceeded to the point and copied
down the characters:- 【中国打日本】 which when translated
reads "China fights the Japanese Army".

Enquiries were made in the vicinity in an
effort to locate the writer without success.

A search of the District was made but no
other slogans were found.

Slogans washed off the property by station
coolie.

With reference to the handbill of anti-Japanese
nature found in the vicinity of the New World, Bubbling
Well and Yu Ya Ching Roads at about 5 p.m. April 29,
which purports to have been written by one Kazuo
Aoyama, a Japanese of the Japanese Democratic Party,
I have to state that enquiries were carried out at the
Japanese Military Police and the following information
obtained:-

So far the identity of the person named Kazuo
Aoyama is not known, but it is believed that the above
is a pen-name used by a certain Japanese or a Chinese
who has a good knowledge of the Japanese language.
He is believed to reside in Hongkong or Chungking and
undertakes propaganda work in favour of the National
Government of China in cooperation with a Japanese
named Wataru Kaji, who shortly after the outbreak of
the current sino-Japanese hostilities, proceeded from
Shanghai to Hankow via Hongkong and Canton. Some
time ago the Japanese censors in the Post Office
confiscated mail containing anti-war literature in
Japanese, which had the name Kazuo Aoyama and according
to the Military Police judging from the composition &
style of the literature, it is believed to have been
written by a Japanese.

D. Kamashita
D. S.

D.C. (Special Branch)

REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. Date MAY 1, 1939.）

Subject. Anti-Japanese Propaganda.

Made /by/ and Forwarded by D.I. Crawford

A handbill printed in the Chinese language of an anti-Japanese nature which attacks the Japanese Military, was found outside the New World Building, Bubbling Well Road at 5 p.m., April 29. The handbill is printed over the name of an alleged Japanese subject who claims to be a member of the Democratic Party. A translation of this handbill reads as follows:-

"Dear Chinese Brethren,

While Fascism is threatening world peace, the Chinese people are conducting a sacred war of resistance for the purpose of upholding justice and humanity. They are not only striving for their own existence and liberty but also endeavouring to hasten the awakening of Japan towards cooperation with new China in the formation of a united peace front in the Far East. We therefore recognize the brave Chinese warriors as our friends. Although the Japanese militarists have "robbed" China of much land and property, they will soon find that their end is near because they are sinking deeper and deeper into "mud pools" and will not be able to extricate themselves.

Let all patriotic Chinese rise up and put an end to the aggressive war by Japan by overthrowing the Japanese militarists! Let us work for world peace and racial emancipation! Let the Japanese revolution be assured! Long live the Republic of China.

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特务科登记处 编号 S. B. D. 日期 1939年5月1日。）

事由：反日宣传。

由警探长克劳福德（Crawford）制作并转呈

1939年4月29日下午5时，在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）新世界大楼外发现一份中文印刷的反日传单，该传单攻击日本军队。传单署名为一名自称是民主党成员的所谓日本籍人士。该传单的译文如下：-

“亲爱的中国同胞们，

当法西斯主义威胁世界和平时，中国人民正在进行一场神圣的抗战，以维护正义与人道。他们不仅为自己的生存和自由而奋斗，还致力于促使日本觉醒，与新中华合作，在远东建立统一的和平阵线。因此，我们将勇敢的中国战士视为朋友。虽然日本军国主义者‘掠夺’了中国的大量土地和财产，但他们很快会发现末日临近，因为他们正越陷越深地陷入‘泥潭’，无法自拔。

让所有爱国的中国人奋起，推翻日本军国主义者，终结日本的侵略战争！让我们为世界和平与种族解放而努力！祝日本革命成功！中华民国万岁。

Date April 12, 1939.

Subject Letter containing national salvation propaganda
received by the Kashing Road Police Station
through the mail on March 23.

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C Crawford J. S

With reference to the attached report of
Kashing Road Police Station (Misc. 16/39) dated March 24,
on the subject of a letter received at that station
on March 23, containing two pamphlets of a national
salvation nature, full translations of these pamphlets
have been made and are forwarded as Appendix "A" and "B".

One of the pamphlets, which is printed in black,
condemns the Japanese for utilizing the names of Chinese
patriotic organizations to hoodwink the general public
in furtherance of their subversive activities and
exhorts local Chinese residents to guard against the
activities of bogus organizations.

The other pamphlet, printed in red, urges
the Chinese people in every walk of life to give their
unwavering support to the present war of resistance
in order to further strengthen the national morale with
a view to attaining final victory.

For the purpose of finding out the origin
of the propaganda, Special Branch detectives have
visited all printing plants in the International
Settlement and also made enquiries among the printers
but without success.

Kao Yen-ken
D. S. I.

FILE
D. C. (Special Branch).

参照附件中嘉兴路警署于3月24日提交的报告（杂项 16/39），关于该警署于3月23日收到的一封包含两份救国性质小册子的信件，现将这些小册子的完整译文作为附录“A”和“B”转呈。

其中一份用黑色印刷的小册子，谴责日本人利用中国爱国团体的名义来蒙蔽公众，以推进其颠覆活动，并敦促当地中国居民警惕假冒组织的活动。

另一份用红色印刷的小册子，呼吁各界中国人民坚定不移地支持当前的抗战，以进一步加强民族士气，从而取得最终胜利。

为了查明宣传品的来源，特务科侦探走访了公共租界内的所有印刷厂，并向印刷商进行了查询，但均未获成功。

page_data.en:
Appendix "A"

Translation of a handbill (Printed in black and classified
as "1") which was received by the Nanking Road Station by
post on March 23, 1938.
............

Since the withdrawal of the National Troops from
the Shanghai area, the 4,500,000 Chinese residents in the
Settlement and the French Concession have been under the
protection of the S.M.C. and C.M.F. over a period of one
year. The attitude of the Municipal authorities in
dealing with the present situation deserves the respect
of all. Fortunately, the majority of the people
appreciate this peace and order, with the exception of
a few undesirables, who however, appear to have not been
bold enough to openly challenge public opinion.

Recently an alarming piece of news was received
that the Japanese invaders are employing unruly elements
at a high pay for the purpose of creating disturbances.
They use the titles of patriotic organizations to hoodwink
the public in the furtherance of their activities, but
their tricks do not escape the attention of the
intelligentsia.

The Japanese instigate Chinese bad elements to
conduct radical activities under an anti-Japanese cloak
in the Settlement and French Concession in an endeavour
to seize the opportunity of taking independent action.
Judging from the above, the Japanese appear to have the
intention of exterminating the 4,500,000 people once and
for all, and are endeavouring to make a third party the
instrument for their project. It is hoped that the
residents in Shanghai shall keep away from any
organizations of a suspicious character, and that the
young students particularly should beware of being
utilized by the enemy.
page_data.zh:
附录“A”

1938年3月23日南京路警署通过邮递收到的一份传单（黑色印刷，归类为“1”）的译文 ____ 

自从国军撤离上海地区以来，租界和法租界的450万中国居民在工部局和法公董局的保护下已度过了一年。市政当局在处理当前局势时的态度值得所有人尊重。幸运的是，大多数人珍视这种和平与秩序，除了少数不良分子，但他们似乎也不敢公然挑战舆论。

最近收到一则令人震惊的消息，称日本入侵者高薪雇佣不法之徒制造骚乱。他们利用爱国团体的头衔来蒙蔽公众，以推进其活动，但这些伎俩并未逃过知识界的注意。

日本人煽动中国不良分子在租界和法租界披着反日的外衣进行激进活动，企图伺机采取独立行动。从上述情况判断，日本人似乎意图一举消灭这450万人民，并试图利用第三方作为其计划的工具。希望上海居民远离任何可疑性质的组织，特别是年轻学生应警惕被敌人利用。

page_data.en:
Appendix "B"
Translation of a pamphlet received by the Kashing
Road Police Station by post on March 23, 1939.
(Printed in red and classified as "2").

It goes without saying that the only way for China to
maintain her very existence under the present circumstances
is through war, but the question of how this war is to be
effectively waged is of paramount importance and truly
deserves our serious consideration. When all relevant
factors regarding the present military situation are taken
into account, we cannot but come to the natural conclusion
that equal significance and value should be attached to
both positional and mobile warfare of a nation-wide scale.
The Japanese Government have already put in effect
their National Mobilization Bill. By the term 'mobilization'
is meant a war of attrition by the contest of combined
national strength. It is a contest of economic endurance,
cultural leadership, political unity and military strength
combined together. Hence for our country, if final victory
is to be gained it is more than imperative now that the efforts
of all men, be they economic experts, cultural leaders,
political genius or military strategists, should be
concentrated and utilized to the fullest possible extent
in order to ensure cooperation in their various fields
of patriotic endeavour. We should be determined to leave
no stone unturned in our task of bringing about and
continually augmenting the strength of this cooperation
because the bitter and heart-rending memory must be
constantly borne in mind that the Sung and Ming Dynasties
were subjected to alien aggression and finally capitulated
centuries ago not because of their lack of loyal and efficient
generals or patriotic and hard-fighting soldiers in the
field, but because, sad to relate, they had in their courts
and palaces a vast number of cowards and turncoats who were
holding key positions of the state and who surrendered their
all, almost as soon as the least pressure was brought
page_data.zh:
附录“B”
1939年3月23日嘉兴路警署通过邮递收到的一份小册子的译文。
（红色印刷，归类为“2”）。

不言而喻，在当前形势下，中国维持生存的唯一途径是通过战争，但如何有效进行这场战争的问题至关重要，确实值得我们认真考虑。当考虑到当前军事局势的所有相关因素时，我们不得不得出自然的结论，即全国范围的阵地战和运动战应具有同等的重要性和价值。日本政府已经实施了《国家总动员法》。所谓“动员”，是指综合国力较量的消耗战。这是经济耐力、文化领导力、政治统一和军事力量相结合的综合较量。因此，对于我国而言，如果要取得最终胜利，现在比以往任何时候都更迫切需要将所有人的努力集中并充分利用，无论是经济专家、文化领袖、政治天才还是军事战略家，以确保他们在各个爱国努力领域的合作。我们应下定决心，不遗余力地促成并不断增强这种合作的力量，因为必须时刻铭记那痛苦且令人心碎的记忆：宋明两代在数百年前遭受外来侵略并最终投降，并非因为缺乏忠诚高效的将领或爱国善战的士兵，而是可悲的是，他们的朝廷和宫殿中有大量占据国家关键职位的懦夫和叛徒，他们几乎在受到 slightest pressure（轻微压力）时就交出了一切

page_data.en:
(2)

to bear upon them. The same may be said of the Taiping
Rebellion against the Ching Regime.

It is to be hoped that our fellow compatriots will
turn to good advantage the benefit of these historical
lessons gained at such disastrous cost.

----
page_data.zh:
(2)

施加于他们身上。太平天国反抗清廷的情况也是如此。

希望我们的同胞能充分利用这些以惨重代价换来的历史教训。

----

page_data.en:
THE WAR FOR THE WHOLE NATION

In connection with the situation in China, it is quite
obviously that the only way we can exist is to keep on fighting,
otherwise China will be overthrown. We know we must fight,
but the question regarding how to keep on fighting is an
important problem, which is due for consideration.

If we fight on a small scale we can secure victory in
some places, but we never can reach the final victory. On the
other hand if we fight on a large scale, we can do so over a
wide area, and this fighting is more effective. The military
situation is bound to change at any moment, so we must adopted
both the large and small scale of fighting.

The Japanese have mobilized their nation to fight against
us, therefore, we must have a definite plan to meet them. We
must have a "War of the whole nation", which means that we must
mobilize all the economical, cultural, political and military
experts, and as a result of their joint co-operation we will
be successful. The fighting units in the front line are, of
course, a part of our plan. The experts must remember to work
hard and not to give up at the half way, and the most important
principle is co-operation.

We hope that the important leaders of this "War of the whole
nation" will not only select all the experts to do their part, but
also try to make every one of the 400,000,000 Chinese understand
that to destroy the enemy, they must be attacked from various
points. In doing so the enemy never can occupy our territory.

It is further desired that persons to be rewarded or punished
must be dealt with in a fair manner, and the important people of
this war must be not jealous of others. They must co-operate in
every way.

That, the Sung and Ming Dynasties were overthrown, was a
result of traitors who was ruling the countries at that time, and who
tried to compromise with their enemies, therefore, the military
force is not to be blamed.

The result of the Tai Ping Rebellion being defeated by
the Qing Dy
page_data.zh:
全民抗战

鉴于中国局势，显而易见，我们生存的唯一途径就是坚持战斗，否则中国将被推翻。我们知道必须战斗，但关于如何坚持战斗的问题是一个重要问题，值得考虑。

如果我们进行小规模战斗，我们可以在某些地方取得胜利，但我们永远无法取得最终胜利。另一方面，如果我们进行大规模战斗，我们可以在广阔的区域进行，这种战斗更为有效。军事局势随时可能发生变化，因此我们必须采取大规模和小规模战斗相结合的方式。

日本人已动员其全国力量与我们作战，因此，我们必须有明确的计划来应对他们。我们必须进行“全民抗战”，这意味着我们必须动员所有经济、文化、政治和军事专家，通过他们的通力合作，我们将获得成功。前线的作战部队当然是我们计划的一部分。专家们必须记住要努力工作，不要半途而废，最重要的原则是合作。

我们希望这场“全民抗战”的重要领导人不仅会选拔所有专家各司其职，还会努力让四亿中国人中的每一个人都明白，要消灭敌人，必须从各个点进行攻击。这样做，敌人就永远无法占领我们的领土。

此外，希望赏罚必须公平处理，这场战争的重要人物不得嫉妒他人。他们必须在各方面进行合作。

宋明两代之所以灭亡，是当时统治国家的奸臣试图与敌人妥协的结果，因此，军队不应受到指责。

太平天国被清王朝击败的结果是

All Chinese must bear in mind that the end of above results
is always misery. (Not signed)

Enemy's Scheme

Since the withdrawal of the Chinese National Troops, the
4,500.000 Chinese in Shanghai were protected by the Shanghai Municipal
Council and the French Authorities for more than one year. They
have tried their best to meet the serious situation, and the Chinese
also behaved themselves as good citizens. Amongst those there are,
of course, some unscrupulous Chinese, but they were not very active,
because they feared that if they exposed themselves they would become
the public enemies.

At present news is being circulated that the Japanese have
hired some undesirable Chinese to make trouble. This is obviously
understood by every one.

Their second step is to instruct the unscrupulous Chinese
to use violent means and actions in the name of the Chinese Patriotic
Society, whereby the Japanese can take opportunity of these incidents
and do as they like, and thus they can victimize all the Chinese in
Shanghai.

We hope that the Chinese will not take an active part in these
purported "Patriotic Societies", and furthermore all the students will
bear in mind that they must behave themselves and not to be utilized
by the enemy. By doing so, although the Japanese use cunning, yet
they can do nothing.

J. M. Ross
24/3/39. Not signed.

其将领之间缺乏合作。
所有中国人都必须牢记，上述结果带来的总是苦难。（未署名）

敌人的阴谋

自从中国正规军撤离后，上海的四百五十万中国人在过去一年多里一直受到上海公共租界工部局和法国当局的保护。他们已尽力应对严峻局势，中国人也表现得像好公民一样。其中当然有一些无良之徒，但他们并不十分活跃，因为他们担心如果暴露自己，就会成为公敌。

目前流传的消息称，日本人雇佣了一些不良分子制造麻烦。这一点显然为大家所理解。

他们的第二步是指使无良之徒以“中华爱国社”的名义使用暴力手段和行动，以便日本人利用这些事件为所欲为，从而迫害上海的所有中国人。

我们希望中国人不要积极参与这些所谓的“爱国社团”，此外，所有学生都要牢记，必须约束自己的行为，不要被敌人利用。这样做，虽然日本人狡诈，但也无可奈何。

J. M. Ross
1939年3月24日。未署名。

Translation of a handbill entitled "Intrigues of the Enemy"
........

Since the withdrawal of the National Troops from
the Shanghai Area, the 4,500,000 Chinese residents in the
Settlement and the French Concession have been under the
protection of the S.M.C. and C.M.F. over a period of one
year. The attitude of the two Municipal Authorities in
dealing with the present situation deserves the respect
of all. Fortunately, the majority of the people
appreciate this peace and order, with the exception of
a few undesirables, who, however, appear to have not been
bold enough to openly challenge public opinion.

Recently an alarming piece of news was received
that the Japanese invaders are employing unruly elements
at a high pay for the purpose of creating disturbances.
They use the titles of patriotic organizations to hoodwink
the public in the furtherance of their activities, but
their tricks do not escape the attention of the
intelligentsia.

The Japanese instigate Chinese bad elements to
conduct radical activities under an anti-Japanese cloak
in the Settlement and French Concession in an endeavour
to seize the opportunity of taking independent action.
Judging from the above, the Japanese appear to have the
intention of exterminating the 4,500,000 people once and
for all, and are endeavouring to make a third party the
instrument for their project. It is hoped that the
residents in Shanghai shall keep away from any
organizations of a suspicious character, and that the
young students particularly should beware of being
utilized by the enemy.

题为《敌人之阴谋》的传单译文
 ____ 

自从国民军撤出上海地区以来，租界和法租界的四百五十万中国居民在一年多的时间里一直受到上海公共租界工部局和法公董局的保护。两个市政当局在处理当前局势时的态度值得所有人尊重。幸运的是，大多数人珍视这种和平与秩序，除了少数不良分子，然而，这些人似乎还没有大胆到公然挑战舆论的地步。

最近收到一则令人震惊的消息，日本侵略者正以高薪雇佣不法之徒，目的是制造骚乱。他们利用爱国组织的名义来蒙蔽公众，以推进其活动，但他们的伎俩并未逃过知识分子的注意。

日本人煽动中国不良分子在租界和法租界披着反日的外衣进行激进活动，企图抓住机会采取独立行动。从上述情况判断，日本人似乎意图一举消灭这四百万人口，并试图使第三方成为其计划的工具。希望上海居民远离任何可疑性质的组织，特别是年轻学生应警惕被敌人利用。

Date December 31, 1938.

Subject National Salvation Propaganda

Made by D.S.I. Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C. Clausen (J)

At 11 p.m., December 30, copies of a coloured
handbill of an anti-Japanese nature were found in the
Skating Rink of the Wing On Company and also on Nanking
Road near Chekiang Road. It purports to emanate from
the "China Youth Anti-Japanese and National Salvation
Group" ( 中國青年抗日救亡團 ) and is in the form
of a letter calling upon the Chinese youth in this
"isolated island" to fulfil their duty in the defence of
the country.

The handbill rabidly denounces the Japanese
militarists for their ambition to ruin China, and holds
them responsible for the atrocities perpetrated by their
soldiers on China's soil. It draws the attention of the
Chinese juveniles to the fact that with the blood of the
Chinese gallant soldiers under the leadership of
Generalissimo Chiang, China has been able to resist
barbarous Japan for a period more than one year. The
dream of the 'enemy' to conclude the war within the shortest
period has been practically shattered. With the
mobilization of all her military forces, as well as
political and economical strength, the handbill adds,
Japan has so far obtained nothing but a few cities along
the communication lines in China. The literature
alleges that Japan is now on the verge of collapse in
view of the huge national debt sustained by the Japanese
people as the result of the Conflict.

It concludes by advising the Chinese in Shanghai
to participate in the struggle on their own initiative.

制作人：副督察高延根（Kao Yen-ken） 转呈人：C. Clausen (J)

12月30日晚11时，在永安公司溜冰场以及南京路靠近浙江路处，发现了反日性质的彩色传单副本。该传单声称出自“中国青年抗日救亡团”（中國青年抗日救亡團），形式为一封信，呼吁身处此“孤岛”的中国青年履行保卫国家的职责。

该传单猛烈谴责日本军国主义者毁灭中国的野心，并认为其士兵在中国土地上犯下的暴行应由他们负责。它提请中国青年注意这样一个事实：在蒋委员长的领导下，凭借中国英勇将士的鲜血，中国已能够抵抗野蛮的日本长达一年多。“敌人”在最短时间内结束战争的梦想实际上已经破灭。传单补充说，尽管日本动员了其全部军事力量以及政治和经济实力，但迄今为止，除了占领中国交通线沿线的几座城市外，一无所获。该文献声称，鉴于日本人民因冲突而背负巨额国债，日本现已处于崩溃的边缘。

最后，它建议上海的中国人主动参与斗争。

Anti Japanese slogan chalked at Electric

At 2.30p.m. on the 28-12-38 a telephone message
was received from Detective Sergeant Hiramatsu attached
to the Special Branch of the Japanese Consular Police to
the effect that several kinds of Anti Japa nese slogan has
been chalked at the electric pole at outside No. 327
Kiangse Road.

D.S.I. Kobayashi and C.D.S. 118 immediately proceed-
ed to the above location and discovered the slogan "Down
with Japanese Imperialism" was chalked at the electric
poles at the east side of Kiangse Road between Ningpo
Road and Tientsin Road. The writing was written in a
poor handwriting.

Enquiries in the vicinity failed to obtain any
information which would lead to identity of the person
responsible for writing of the slogan.

The writing was washed off the pole in the presence
of the undersigned by station coolie.

The undersigned interviewed Mr. Zee Tien Ling (徐天林) Secretary of the Pootung Guild, 1454 Avenue Edward VII re persons admitted to the roof garden of the building. Mr. Zee explained that the entrances to the roof garden were usually kept locked and closed, but on the date in question, the roof garden was open for several hours for the purpose of cleaning and dust- ing floor mats, and the coolies engaged in this task had omitted to secure the entrance to the roof garden after leaving. 1/Sheet No. 2.

More than one year has elapsed since the resistance
of war was offered by China. During this period, it is
grievous to say that the stubborn enemy has sent their
whole army to China, trampled our soil, stole our
property and raped our women.
Fortunately, under the leadership of our Generali-
ssimo Chiang Kai Shek, we have been able to shelter
their dream and we will continue to resist the aggressors
so long as the war exists. Now the war has come to its
second phase and needless to point out, a new plan has
been duly made by our highest authorities, but at the
beginning of the new year, we wish to consult you all
also on this same subject. We hope you youths living
in this land are able to carry out your holy duties.
Although Japan has the chemical warfares with
which to suppress China, who is her old neighbour, of
the same race, its gamble in this respect has neverthe-
less proved abortive. Their net gain so far is that
they have suffered appreciable losses both in men and
money. They have had to change their slogan too - "To
crush China in a short period" is amended to read "war
for 10 or 100 years." The further inland they go the
nearer they will be to extermination.
During the struggle, the New China has nevertheless
become stronger and stronger. In every dynasty, youth
is the main body of the nation. Whenever war breaks
out, youths are always found standing in the front line
fighting bravely without regard for their lives, hence
their glorious record in history. Since the outbreak
of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, millions of Chinese
youths have gone to the front lines shed their hot
blood and sacrificed their lives resulting in the enemy
becoming apprehensive. Although Japan has become
weakened in power, the way to ultimate victory is still
far removed. We should grasp the final chance to
complete our mission. Heaven helps those who help
themselves. Don't depend too much on foreign nations.
Our sole purpose is "Our nation is superior."
Regardless of religion or thoughts, every youth, if he
is not idle, dismayed or crazy, ought to join our group
and help us carry our our great work. Many weak points
have been observed in the occupied areas and we have to
concentrate our minds on covering these points. We
must organize a sound body in order to utilize our
endless power and assist in driving the enemies back to
their homes.
My dear people, we have suffered enough from our
enemies. Be brave ! Be brave ! Rise up ! Rise up !
page_data.zh:
1/页码 No. 2.

中国进行抗战已有一年多。在此期间，令人痛心的是，顽固的敌人将其全军派往中国，践踏我们的国土，掠夺我们的财产，强奸我们的妇女。
幸运的是，在我们蒋中正委员长的领导下，我们得以粉碎他们的梦想，只要战争存在，我们将继续抵抗侵略者。现在战争已进入第二阶段，毋庸赘言，我国最高当局已妥善制定新计划，但在新的一年伊始，我们也希望就同一主题征求各位的意见。我们希望生活在这片土地上的青年们能够履行你们的神圣职责。
虽然日本拥有化学战手段来镇压作为其老邻居、同种族的中国，但其在此方面的赌博终究证明是失败的。他们目前的净收益是人员在金钱方面都遭受了重大损失。他们也不得不改变口号——“在短时间内粉碎中国”已修改为“战争持续10年或100年”。他们深入内地越远，就越接近灭亡。
在斗争中，新中国 nevertheless 变得越来越强大。在每个朝代，青年都是国家的主体。每当战争爆发，青年总是站在前线，不顾生死英勇作战，因此在历史上留下了光辉的记录。自中日敌对行动爆发以来，数百万中国青年奔赴前线，洒下热血，牺牲生命，致使敌人感到恐惧。虽然日本国力已削弱，但通往最终胜利的道路仍然遥远。我们应该抓住最后的机会来完成我们的使命。天助自助者。不要过分依赖外国。我们唯一的目的就是“我族优越”。
无论宗教或思想如何，每个青年，如果不懒惰、不沮丧或不疯狂，都应该加入我们的团体，帮助我们开展伟大的工作。在占领区已观察到许多弱点，我们必须集中精力弥补这些弱点。我们必须组织一个健全的团体，以便利用我们无穷的力量，协助将敌人赶回他们的家园。
亲爱的同胞们，我们受敌人的苦难已经够多了。勇敢点！勇敢点！起来！起来！

Date May 23rd 1938.

〔印：REPORT CONFIDENTIAL〕

Subject Anti-Japanese Posters.

Made by D.S.I. Shih Ssu-chien Forwarded by C. Crawford

The following hand-written posters of an anti-Japanese nature were seen posted on the outside wall of N.W.K. No.9 Cotton Mill, 640 Markham Road (Gordon Road District) at 7 a.m. May 23rd. Translation is as follows:-

(1). Down with Japanese Imperialists.
To win a battle through the aid of poison gas is nothing to be proud of.
We'll kill our enemies courageously. This will win the admiration of the people of the world. The deeds committed by our enemies have become the object of attacks by all countries in the world.

(2). Beat the Japanese with an undaunted spirit.
To win a battle with poison gas is laughable.

(3). The shameless dwarf slaves massacre the innocent civilians and use poison gas which is contrary to International Law. Their action are deplorable. Let us unite!

N.B. Those who tear down the above posters are sons of the Japanese.

主题 反日海报。

由副助理督察长施士坚制作 经 C. Crawford 转呈

5月23日上午7时，在戈登路区马克姆路640号西北国棉九厂的外墙上，发现张贴了以下手写反日海报。译文如下：-

(1). 打倒日本帝国主义者。
依靠毒气赢得战斗没什么可骄傲的。
我们将英勇杀敌。这将赢得世界人民的钦佩。敌人的行径已成为世界各国攻击的对象。

(2). 以大无畏的精神打击日本人。
用毒气赢得战斗是可笑的。

(3). 无耻的矮奴屠杀无辜平民，并使用违反国际法的毒气。他们的行为令人痛惜。让我们团结起来！

注意：撕毁上述海报者是日本人的儿子。

Sir,

The attached posters of an anti-Japanese nature were
found posted on the wall of the N.C.K.No.9 Mill,Koji Road
at 11 a.m. 23/5/38.

Translations are as follows:-

(1) "Dwarf-Slaves" spread poison gas which action is against
International Law. They have also massacred innocent
people. This action is hated by every one. Therefore
our multitude should unite together to:
overthrow Japanese Imperialism! Victory by poison gas
should not be admired.
The bravery of our soldiers is much praised by all
nations.

(2) To persevere to the end to gain victory over Japanese.

(3) The spreading of poison gas is to be laughed.

〔此处为手写签名〕
D. S. I.

D.D.O."B" Division.

附件中的反日海报于1938年5月23日上午11时发现张贴在柯基路西北国棉九厂的墙上。

译文如下：-

(1) “矮奴”散布毒气，此举违反国际法。他们还屠杀无辜百姓。此行为为众人所憎恨。因此，我大众应团结起来：
推翻日本帝国主义！靠毒气取得的胜利不应被钦佩。
我军之英勇受到各国高度赞扬。

(2) 坚持到底以战胜日本人。

(3) 散布毒气之举可笑。

〔此处为手写签名〕
副助理督察长

Translation of a handbill entitled “Intrigues of the Enemy" 

Since the withdrawal of the National Troops from 
the Shanghai Area, the 4,500,000 Chinese residats in the 
Settlement and the French Concession have been under the 
protection of the S-M.C. and C.M.F. over a period of one 
year. The attitude of the two Municipal Authorities in 
dealing with the present situation deserves the respect 
of all. Fortunately, the majority of the people 
appreciate this peace and orcer, with the exception of 
a few undesirables, who, however, appear to have not been 
bold enough to openly challenge public opinion. 

Recently an alarming piece of news was received 
that the Japanese invaders are employing unruly elements 
at a high pay for the purpose of creating disturbances. 
They use the titles of patriotic organizations to hoodwink 
the public in the furtherance of their activities, but 
their tricks do not escape the attention of the 
intelligentsia. 

The Japanese instigate Chinese bad elements to 
conduct radical activities under an anti-Japanese cloak 
in the Settlenent and French Concession in an endeavour 
to seize the opportunity of taking independent action. 
Judging from the above, the Japanese appear to have the 
intention of exterminating the 4,500,000 people once and 
for all, and are endeavouring to make a third party the 
instrument for their project. It is hoped that the 
residents in Shanghai shall keep away from any 
organizations of a suspicious character, and that the 
young students particularly should beware of being 
utilized by the enemy.

Date December 31, ,.38, 


At ll pem., December 20, copies of a coloured 
handbill of an anti-Japanese nature were found in the 
Skating Rink of the Wing On Company and also on Nanking 
Road near Chekiang Road. It purports to emanate from 
the "China Youth Anti-Japanese and National Salvation 
Group" ( +A@F fio Ade pa ) and is in the form 
of a letter calling upon the Chinese youth in this 
®isolated island” to fulfil their duty in the defence of 
the country. 

The handbill rabidly denounces the Japanese 
militariets for their ambition to ruin China, and holds 
them responsible for the atrocities perpetrated by their 


soldiers on China's soil. It draws the attention of the 


Chinese juveniles to the fact that with the blood of the 
Chinese gallant soldiers under the leadership of 
Generalissimo Chiang, China has been able to resist 
barbarous Japan for a period more than one year. The 
dream of the'enemy'to conclude the war within the shortest 
period has been practically shattered. With ‘he 
mobilization of all her military forces, as well as 
political and economical strength, the handbill adds, 
Japan hes so far obtained nothing but a few cities along 
the communication lines in China. The literature 
alleges that Japan is now on the verge of collapse in 


view of the huge national debt sustained by the Japanese 
people as the result of the Conflict. 
It concludes by advising the Chinese in Shanghai 


to participate in the struggle on their own initiative
